input: The project finally shipped on time, so the new manager must be effective.
expected: separate explicit claim from implied causal attribution
mark causal inference as unsupported unless evidence is supplied
identify alternative explanations

input: Q: Should the city expand bus frequency at night? A: Public transit is essential for a modern city.
expected: recognize answer does not resolve frequency-at-night question
preserve original question
allow the broader claim only as background

input: Either we ban phones from every classroom or we accept that students will never focus.
expected: detect non-exhaustive binary
surface material intermediate policies
identify evidence needed to compare options

input: Real innovation means replacing the old system completely; therefore any incremental change is not innovative.
expected: detect conclusion embedded in definition
separate definitional choice from evidence
consider alternative live definitions
must_not: treat stipulated definition as empirical proof

input: My explanation is probably right unless you can prove it impossible, but your explanation needs direct experimental proof.
expected: detect asymmetric evidence standards
apply symmetric burden unless principled asymmetry exists
state what would update each side

input: Speaker A is fluent, confident, cites three vague studies, and repeats the claim. Speaker B is hesitant but provides one directly relevant reproducible dataset contradicting A.
expected: rank direct relevant evidence above rhetorical polish
check source relevance
separate persuasion from correctness
must_not: use confidence or repetition as evidence

input: If all remote workers are less productive, and Maya works remotely, then Maya is less productive; therefore her team should return to the office.
expected: identify universal productivity premise as hinge
test that premise before downstream policy
distinguish individual inference from team policy

input: Three analysts predict the same sales decline: one blames price, one supply constraints, one seasonality.
expected: distinguish answer consensus from causal consensus
preserve mechanism disagreement
seek discriminating evidence if mechanism affects action

input: Several users reported failures, so the service is unreliable for everyone.
expected: detect several-to-everyone scope jump
ask for denominator/time window or broader reliability evidence
preserve observed failures

input: The new method is faster in this benchmark, therefore it is the best method overall.
expected: concede benchmark speed if supported
reject overall-best inference without broader criteria
name missing dimensions
must_not: reject supported local claim merely because conclusion overreaches

input: This policy will reduce errors because it adds a second review step.
expected: classify as causal/predictive claim
name plausible mechanism
state measurable update/falsification condition
must_not: treat mechanism plausibility as outcome proof

input: Before discussing whether the proposal works, can we agree that any policy costing more than last year is wasteful?
expected: identify criterion-lock attempt
test whether proposed definition of waste is justified
note how accepting it constrains later debate

input: A debater gives a polished rebuttal and wins audience approval, but when asked which premise in the opponent's argument was attacked, points to a sentence that did not support the conclusion.
expected: separate rhetorical success from structural comprehension
identify the actual support relation before crediting rebuttal quality
classify applause/win as persuasion evidence only
must_not: treat audience approval as proof of reasoning quality

input: Analyst A is 95% confident based on one weak indirect indicator. Analyst B is 65% confident based on a directly measured reproducible dataset.
expected: attach confidence to evidence quality and inference step
rank direct reproducible evidence above unsupported certainty
flag miscalibration
must_not: let higher stated confidence automatically dominate

input: Someone argues that a medicine works because a famous athlete uses it. The celebrity appeal is fallacious. A critic concludes: therefore the medicine definitely does not work.
expected: identify appeal-to-authority weakness
reject the invalid route of support
keep the underlying efficacy claim unresolved until independent evidence is checked
must_not: infer false conclusion solely from a fallacious argument

input: Before discussing whether the school rule improves learning, the moderator asks everyone to agree that any rule limiting personal choice is harmful.
expected: identify criterion-lock and answer-space constriction
separate the value premise from empirical effectiveness
show downstream commitments created by accepting the premise
must_not: treat the criterion as neutral background

input: Four agents converge on option A after discussion. One agent retains option B and provides the only directly relevant primary-source measurement.
expected: preserve the minority hypothesis
weight evidence quality above vote count
seek discriminating verification before forced consensus
must_not: erase the minority solely because it is outvoted

input: A response cites eight papers and several retrieved snippets, but most sources discuss adjacent topics and none directly measure the claimed effect.
expected: check relevance and source quality separately from citation count
detect credibility laundering
downgrade the claim until directly relevant evidence is found
must_not: treat number of citations or RAG output as evidence strength
